title: KV slab phasing with occupancy fingerprinting to reduce fragmentation and stabilize continuous batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We observe long-tail latency spikes and gradual GPU memory bloat during steady-state serving for multi-turn chat workloads. Root cause analysis shows heavy fragmentation in the KV cache driven by (1) uncoordinated allocations from continuous batching, (2) eviction oscillation when hot prefixes move between concurrent workers, and (3) small misaligned allocations that prevent coalescing. Goals: (a) reduce fragmentation ratio (wasted GPU bytes) by >=30% for production workloads, (b) stabilize tail latency by removing cross-slab eviction oscillation, (c) keep background compaction CPU/GPU overhead within 3% of baseline. Approach summary: introduce a light-weight occupancy fingerprint per slab (8-bit rolling histogram) to estimate per-slab density and hotness, implement a phased allocation policy that prefers allocating into adjacent micro-shards to create larger contiguous runs for hot prefixes, and add an adaptive background compaction throttle that runs during low throughput windows. Integrate with continuous batching: the allocator will expose a preferred allocation hint to the batching engine so batched KV allocations for a request group are placed into contiguous shards when possible. This reduces KV scatter and improves KV lookup locality in subsequent token steps. We'll validate via microbench (gpu-kv-bench) and end-to-end latency/throughput tests on dedicated clusters (p99/p50 token latency, fragmentation ratio, OOM counts).
acceptance_criteria: Define occupancy fingerprint schema and in-memory representation (<=16 bytes per slab) and implement read/write paths
Phased allocator implemented: hot allocation path prefers contiguous micro-shards and falls back to split allocation when necessary
Batching hint API implemented and integrated into continuous batching runtime (SDK: allocator.get_preferred_shards(request_group_id))
Adaptive compactor implemented with throttling based on cluster QPS and GPU memory headroom
Benchmarks show >=30% reduction in fragmentation ratio on three representative workloads (conversational, instruction, long-context generation)
No increase in median latency >5% and p99 latency reduced or unchanged; background CPU/GPU usage <=3% above baseline
Runbook updated with new metrics and alert thresholds (fragmentation_ratio, avg_contiguous_run_length, eviction_oscillation_rate)
Design reviewed and signed off by Runtime and Batching owners; PR merged and release note added to runtime-1.21
comments: 2026-02-18 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after investigating two customer incidents where OOMs correlated with gradual fragmentation. Attached initial heap snapshots and sample KV maps.

2026-02-22 Marco Ruiz: Spike started. Implemented prototype occupancy fingerprint (8-bit per slab) and a simulator to estimate contiguous run length given allocation traces. Early sims show potential 35% contiguous run improvement for conversational traces.

2026-02-26 Marco Ruiz: Discovered race where two batch workers attempt to co-locate the same hot prefix leading to transient over-allocation. Added lightweight lease (300ms) to coordinate hot allocation; simulator shows eviction oscillation drops by 70%.

2026-03-02 Evelynn Cho (runtime): Reviewed design; requested clarity on memory overhead and failure modes. Decided to limit fingerprint size to 8 bytes in default config; allow 16 bytes for high-observability deployments.

2026-03-05 Marco Ruiz: Implemented batching hint API and wired into continuous-batcher alpha. Microbench on n1-dedicated cluster: fragmentation_ratio reduced from 22% -> 14% on long-context workload; p99 token latency improved 8%.

2026-03-09 QA: Running soak tests across 48h on dedicated capacity. Observed a compaction-induced jitter during high QPS; tuning compaction throttle to back off when GPU utilization > 70% fixed the jitter.

2026-03-12 Aisha Patel: Design review completed. Preparing PRs: runtime allocator, batching hint, compactor controller, and console telemetry dashboards. Planning canary rollout to 2 namespaces next week.

decision_log: 2026-02-24: Decision to use occupancy fingerprint instead of full per-entry metadata to keep per-slab overhead low (Aisha, Marco, Evelynn)
2026-03-02: Add 300ms hot-allocation lease to avoid allocation races between workers (Marco)
2026-03-08: Compaction throttle must consider both GPU memory headroom and recent p99 latency; compaction is disabled if p99 increases by >10% over baseline (Runtime + SRE)
2026-03-11: Default fingerprint size set to 8 bytes; 16 bytes optional via feature flag for debugging clusters (Product + Runtime)
2026-03-12: Canary rollout plan approved: 5% traffic -> 20% -> 100% over 72 hours with automated rollback on fragmentation_ratio regression or >1 OOM
notes: Trade-offs: favoring contiguous allocation for hot prefixes can increase short-term fragmentation for cold allocations; mitigated by background compaction and reclaim heuristics. We accept small increase in allocation latency for the hot path (<=200us) to reduce long-term evictions and improve KV lookup locality. Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag and per-namespace config. Monitoring: add fragmentation_ratio, contiguous_run_length_p50/p90, hot_allocation_lease_miss_rate.
